Recommendation Detail

Change Materiality Definitions

Significant
The change introduces new obligations or materially strengthens existing ones such that failure to implement would reasonably increase regulatory, customer, or conduct risk.
Moderate
The change introduces new or strengthened requirements that may require updates to processes, controls, reporting, training, or governance in one or more areas.
Minor
The change introduces limited additional expectation (e.g. emphasis, documentation, guidance) but is not expected to materially alter policies, controls, systems, or operating models.
No Change
The obligation is substantively unchanged. Any differences are editorial, structural, clarifying, or re-ordering only, with no change to intent or compliance outcome.

Clause Type Definitions

Obligation
Binding conduct requirements on the general insurer. Includes consumer rights that the insurer must enable or respect.
Scope
Defines applicability, boundaries, declarations, and principles — who and what the Code covers, liability limitations, Code-vs-law hierarchy, and non-binding guidance.
Administrative
Governance, compliance monitoring, reporting structures, cross-references, and Code administration processes.
Definition
Formal term definitions used across the Code (e.g. Business Days, Extraordinary Event, Vulnerability).

Change Type Definitions

New
An obligation that did not exist in any form in the 2020 Code. No prior equivalent, predecessor, or conceptual analog was present.
Updated
The obligation existed in the 2020 Code but has been materially strengthened, expanded, restructured, or had new requirements added in the Draft 2026.
Unchanged
The obligation is substantively the same as the 2020 Code. Any differences are editorial, structural, or clarifying only — no change to intent or compliance outcome.
Removed
The obligation has been explicitly removed from the Draft 2026 Code, typically because it is now covered by legislation or consolidated elsewhere.
